LESSON: VISUAL MEMORY

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.5: Visual memory

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Visual memory. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you see memory learner should be able to: in visual memory games. around class?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya
3. practise Visual memory in clear steps
4. apply Visual memory in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: VISUAL MEMORY
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Visual memory helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: VISUAL MEMORY
Study Visual memory like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Visual memory”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Visual memory to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Visual memory in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Visual memory in clear steps. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Visual memory in clear steps.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Visual memory in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Visual memory in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Visual memory in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Visual memory in one real-life situation this week.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Visual memory”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Visual memory in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Visual memory is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Visual memory”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Visual memory to a partner. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: practise Visual memory in clear steps)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Visual memory”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: apply Visual memory in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Visual memory to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Visual memory in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Visual memory from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Visual memory: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Visual memory?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you see memory learner should be able to: in visual memory games. around class?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Visual memory means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Visual memory means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Visual memory from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
